title: Angles and Parallel Lines: Corresponding, Alternate and Co-interior Angles
seo_title: Year 7 Parallel Lines Worksheets: Corresponding, Alternate and Co-interior Angles (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior relationships between angles formed when parallel lines are crossed by a transversal; use them to solve problems and explain reasons
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on angles and parallel lines for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7M04): corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles, finding unknown angles, equations and reasons. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°.
key_sub: Look for the F, Z and C shapes, and check the lines are parallel.
body_html:
How it works

When a line (a transversal) crosses two parallel lines, eight angles are made, in two sizes.

  • Corresponding angles (F shape) are equal.
  • Alternate angles (Z shape) are equal.
  • Co-interior angles (C shape) add up to 180°.

Always give a reason, such as “alternate angles in parallel lines are equal”. If corresponding or alternate angles are equal, the lines must be parallel.

Example

Find x in the diagram above.

The angles are corresponding (F shape).

Answer: x = 65°

Example

Co-interior angles are 70° and y. Find y.

They add to 180°: 180 − 70.

Answer: y = 110°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking co-interior angles are equal. They add up to 180°.
  • Subtracting from 360° instead of 180°.
  • Mixing up the F, Z and C shapes.
  • Using these rules when the lines are not parallel (look for the arrows).

faq.a: Angles in matching positions at each crossing, like an F shape. When the lines are parallel they are equal.
Angles on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallel lines, like a Z shape. They are equal.
Angles on the same side of the transversal, between the parallel lines, like a C shape. They add up to 180°.

faq.q: How can I tell if two lines are parallel?
faq.a: If a pair of corresponding or alternate angles are equal, or co-interior angles add to 180°, the lines are parallel.

items.q: Alternate angles between parallel lines are 2x + 9 and 53°. Find x.
items.e: Alternate angles are equal: 2x + 9 = 53, so 2x = 44 and x = 22°.

items.q: Which pair of angles are equal when lines are parallel?
items.e: Alternate angles (Z shape) are equal. Co-interior angles add to 180°.

items.q: Which shape helps you spot corresponding angles?
items.e: Corresponding angles sit in matching positions, like an F shape.

items.q: Which shape helps you spot co-interior angles?
items.e: Co-interior angles are on the same side, between the lines: a C shape.

items.q: What do co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to?
items.e: Co-interior angles are supplementary: they add to 180°.

items.q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 72°. Which other angle is NOT possible at either crossing?
items.e: Every angle is either 72° or 180° − 72° = 108°. 100° is not possible.

items.q: Vertically opposite angles are…
items.e: Where two lines cross, opposite angles are always equal.

items.q: A railway track has two parallel rails. A road crosses at 64° to one rail. What angle does it make with the other rail, in the same position?
items.e: Corresponding angles are equal: 64°.

items.q: In a parallelogram one angle is 70°. Using co-interior angles, what is the next angle around the shape?
items.e: Opposite sides are parallel, so neighbouring angles are co-interior: 180 − 70 = 110°.

items.q: Which reason is correct? “Angle x = 55° because…” (the angles form a Z between parallel lines)
c: Angles in a triangle add to 180°
Angles at a point add to 360°
items.e: A Z shape means alternate angles are equal.

items.q: Two angles form a C shape between parallel lines. One is 95°. What is the other?
items.e: Co-interior: 180 − 95 = 85°.

items.q: Ladder rungs are parallel. One rung meets the side rail at 82°. What angle does the next rung make with the rail, on the same side and in the same position?
items.e: Corresponding angles are equal: 82°.

items.q: Why must you check for arrows on the lines before using these rules?
c: The rules only work when the lines are parallel
items.e: Corresponding, alternate and co-interior rules only work when the lines are parallel.

items.q: An angle on a straight line is 38°. What is the other angle on that line?
items.e: Angles on a straight line add to 180°: 142°.

items.q: Lines AB and CD are parallel. Angle ABC is 47° and angle BCD is an alternate angle. What is angle BCD?
items.e: Alternate angles are equal: 47°.

items.q: In a trapezium the two parallel sides are crossed by a slanted side. One angle on that side is 112°. What is the other angle on the same slanted side?
items.e: They are co-interior: 180 − 112 = 68°.

items.q: Corresponding angles are 4x and 3x + 15. Find x.
Co-interior angles are 2x and 3x. What is the larger angle?
How many angles are made when one line crosses two parallel lines?
items.e: 4 at each crossing: 8 angles, with only two different sizes.

items.q: At one crossing a transversal makes an angle of 90° with a parallel line. What is every angle in the diagram?
items.e: All eight angles are 90°.
